To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the United States, through its military and economic policies, contributed to the development of an anti-Americanism that continues to this day.
the presence of American bases, troops and civilians in the British Caribbean, during World War II, led to the development of an aggressive nationalism in the islands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the Second World War upon the political and economic development of the British West Indies.

the impact of the Second World War upon the political, economic and cultural life of the British Caribbean and the impact of the British Caribbean upon American society and culture during that period.
the impact of the Second World War upon the people and governments of the British West Indian islands of Jamaica, Trinidad, British Guiana, Barbados, and British Honduras.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the American military bases and troops in Trinidad and the other islands of the British Caribbean, while not having the effect that had been hoped for, had a considerable impact on the political and economic development of the islands.
American bases in the British Caribbean were not welcomed by the people of these islands.
the American military presence was a major contributing factor to the rise of nationalism in the British Caribbean, but not a decisive one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the United States was a major factor in the development of nationalism in the British Caribbean.

the British Caribbean was the scene of a struggle between two competing ideologies, one American, the other British, both of them seeking to establish their own brand of democracy and freedom in the area.

we have attempted to explain the development of the anti-American movement in the British Caribbean, the causes which gave rise to this movement, the nature of the movement, and the consequences which resulted from this movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the British Caribbean, anti-Americanism was the result of American behavior in the Caribbean, not of anti-Americanism in the islands.
the United States did not, in the British Caribbean, have a “special relationship” with the British.
the British Caribbean was not a passive recipient of the American presence.
